learn.hook: Fold a butterfly picture down the middle. Both halves match perfectly! That fold is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded.
Some shapes have one line of symmetry, some have many, and some have none.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A triangle with all sides equal has 3 lines of symmetry. A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Letters like A, T and V have a standing (vertical) line of symmetry. B, C and E have a lying (horizontal) one. F, L, N and S have none.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Fold H from top to bottom down the middle: the halves match.
Fold H from left to right across the middle: the halves match.
No other fold works.

learn.reallife: Rangoli, the Taj Mahal from the front, leaves and many logos are symmetrical.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded in half 4 ways: up-down, left-right and along both corner-to-corner lines.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: It folds evenly only across the middle in two ways. A corner-to-corner fold does not make the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry, like in a square

quiz.q: Which letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A folds down the middle into two matching halves. F, L and N do not match when folded.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any letter with straight lines is symmetrical

quiz.q: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes the two halves of S match. H, T and E each have at least one line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks S is symmetrical because it looks the same when turned upside down

quiz.q: A triangle has all 3 sides equal. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: You can fold it from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That is 3 lines.

quiz.q: Which letter has a lying (horizontal) line of symmetry, so its top half matches its bottom half?
quiz.explain: B folded from top to bottom matches. A, T and V have only a standing line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up standing (vertical) and lying (horizontal) lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
quiz.explain: H matches when folded down the middle and when folded across the middle. That is 2 lines.
quiz.mistake: Finds only one of the two folds

quiz.q: Which of these has the most lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes matching halves, so a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square has the most because it has 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper heart down the middle and both halves matched! What is that fold line called?
teach.praise: Yes! When both halves match after folding, the fold is a line of symmetry. Gappu loves it!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when Gappu folds? What do we call that line?

learn.hook: Drop some paint on paper, fold it, press and open. A butterfly appears! How?
points: Ink-blot design: put paint on one half, fold along the middle, press and open. The paint copies onto the other half like a mirror image.
The fold line is the line of symmetry of the design.
When folding a paper plane, the first middle fold is its line of symmetry. Both wings should match.
Place a mirror on the line of symmetry of half a picture and you see the whole picture.
A symmetrical plane flies straighter. If one wing is bigger, the plane turns or tips over.

example.q: Ritu folds a paper plane but one wing is bigger than the other. What will probably happen when she throws it?
steps: The plane is not symmetrical.
One side pushes on the air more than the other.
So the plane turns or tips instead of flying straight.
example.answer: It will turn or tip to one side

learn.reallife: Rangoli artists, ink-blot painters and paper-plane champions all use a fold line to make matching halves.

games.title: Make an ink-blot design
items: Fold a paper in half and open it
Drop paint on one half
Fold it again along the same line
Press gently all over
Open to see the matching halves

games.title: Planes and blots
items: The fold in an ink-blot design is a line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
A plane with one big and one small wing flies straight.
Unequal wings make it turn or tip.
A mirror on the line of symmetry shows the whole shape.
The mirror shows the missing half.
In an ink blot, the copy on the other half is exactly the same way round.
It is a mirror image, flipped left to right.
The middle fold of a paper plane helps make both wings equal.
It is the plane's line of symmetry.

quiz.q: In an ink-blot design, what is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: The fold line splits the design into two matching halves.

quiz.q: Paint is put on the left half and the paper is folded. Where does the copy appear?
options: On the right half, flipped like a mirror
quiz.explain: Folding presses the paint onto the other half as a mirror image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the copy is not flipped

quiz.q: Why should both wings of a paper plane be the same?
quiz.explain: A symmetrical plane balances and flies straight.
quiz.mistake: Does not link symmetry to balance

quiz.q: Which fold is the line of symmetry of a paper plane?
options: The first fold down the middle
A fold at one wing tip
quiz.explain: The middle fold divides the plane into two equal halves.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fold that is not in the middle

quiz.q: Ankit places a mirror along the middle of half a butterfly drawing. What does he see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the other matching half, so the whole butterfly appears.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a mirror shows

quiz.q: An ink-blot design has 6 dots on the left half before folding (none on the fold). How many dots after opening?
quiz.explain: Each dot is copied to the right half: 6 + 6 = 12.

quiz.q: A plane drifts to the left every time. What is likely wrong?
quiz.explain: Unequal (not symmetrical) wings make a plane turn.

quiz.q: A mirror is placed on the line of symmetry of half the letter A. What letter do you see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the missing half, completing the A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror shows a different letter

teach.ask: Gappu wants to make a butterfly painting with matching wings. Explain how folding helps.
teach.praise: Paint one half, fold and press, and the wings match like a mirror. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: What does folding do to the paint on one half?

learn.hook: Put a mirror on half a picture and, like magic, the whole picture appears!
points: A mirror shows a flipped copy. Left becomes right and right becomes left.
If you know one half of a symmetrical shape, you can draw the other half like a mirror image.
Each point on one side is the same distance from the mirror line as its partner on the other side.
Fold paper, cut a shape on the fold and open it. You get a symmetrical shape!
In a mirror, b looks like d.

example.q: Half of a rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line, and no dots on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
steps: The right half is a mirror copy of the left half.
So it also has 7 dots.

learn.reallife: Mehendi designs, kite patterns and paper cut-outs for Diwali use mirror halves.

games.title: Mirror magic
items: In a mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand.
A mirror flips left and right.
The letter b looks like d in a mirror held to its side.
The bump flips to the other side.
The mirror half of a shape can be a different size.
Mirror halves are exactly the same size and shape.
If you cut a half-heart on a fold and open the paper, you get a whole heart.
The fold is the line of symmetry.
The word MOM looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
M and O look the same flipped, and the word reads the same both ways.
The letter F looks the same in a mirror held to its side.
F faces the other way in the mirror.

items.text: Left half has 5 petals and none are on the line. The whole flower has ___ petals.
A half-shape is 3 squares wide. The full shape is ___ squares wide.
In a mirror held to the side, the letter d looks like ___.
A dot is 2 squares to the left of the mirror line. Its mirror dot is 2 squares to the ___.

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper in half and cuts out half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
quiz.explain: The fold is the line of symmetry. Opening it shows both matching halves joined: a whole heart.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the fold joins the two halves

quiz.q: In a mirror held to its side, what does the letter b look like?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The bump of b moves to the left side, making it look like d.
quiz.mistake: Flips it upside down instead of left to right

quiz.q: A symmetrical rangoli has 7 dots on the left of the fold line and none on the line. How many dots are in the whole rangoli?
quiz.explain: The right half is a mirror copy, so it has 7 dots too. 7 + 7 = 14.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: M and O look the same when flipped, and MOM reads the same both ways. B, D, S, N and P do not.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one letter of the word

quiz.q: Which digit looks the same in a mirror held to its side?
quiz.explain: 8 has a standing line of symmetry, so its mirror image is the same. 2, 4 and 7 face the other way.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the digit flipped left to right

quiz.q: Arjun draws the left half of a symmetrical shape. It is 3 squares wide. How wide is the full shape?
quiz.explain: The right half is the same width as the left half. 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the half is already the whole shape

quiz.q: A dot is 4 squares to the left of a mirror line. Where is its mirror dot?
options: 4 squares to the right of the line
4 squares to the left of the line
8 squares to the right of the line
quiz.explain: A mirror dot is the same distance from the line but on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the distance instead of keeping it the same

quiz.q: Kabir stands 2 steps in front of a mirror. How far behind the mirror does his image seem to be?
quiz.explain: Your mirror image always seems to be the same distance behind the mirror as you are in front of it.

teach.ask: Gappu has half a butterfly drawing and a mirror. How can Gappu see or draw the whole butterfly?
teach.praise: Magic! Put the mirror on the line and the other half appears, the same but flipped. Gappu's butterfly is complete!
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to a picture? How is the other half related to the first half?

topics.title: Holes and cuts: predict the pattern

learn.hook: Fold a paper twice, snip a corner, and open it. Will you get one hole or four?
points: Folding once makes 2 layers. A cut away from the fold makes 2 holes; a cut on the fold makes 1 hole.
Folding twice makes 4 layers. A cut in the middle (away from all folds) makes 4 holes.
A cut at the corner where both folds meet makes 1 hole in the centre of the paper.
A cut on just one folded edge (not the corner) makes 2 holes.
To get a square hole, fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner, the same distance along both folds.

example.q: A paper is folded twice. A small half-circle is cut on one folded edge, away from the corner. How many holes after opening?
steps: Folded twice means 4 layers.
On a fold, the 4 layers pair up into 2 holes.
So there are 2 holes.

learn.reallife: Paper snowflakes and paper lanterns for Diwali are made by folding and cutting. The more folds, the more holes!

games.title: Cut and count the holes
pairs: 1 fold, cut away from the fold
2 folds, cut at the folded corner

games.title: Predict the cut
items: Folding twice makes 4 layers.
Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4.
One fold and a cut away from the fold gives 1 hole.
The cut goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.
Cutting straight across the twice-folded corner can make a square hole.
The 4 corner pieces open into a square.
Folding three times makes 6 layers.
2, 4, then 8 layers.
A half-circle cut on the fold opens into a full circle.
The two halves join at the fold.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a half-circle cut on the fold. What do you see when you open it?
quiz.explain: The half-circle on the fold opens into one full circle.

quiz.q: A paper folded once has a small hole punched away from the fold. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a hole punched in the middle, away from all folds. How many holes after opening?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so 4 holes.
steps: 2 folds → 4 layers
4 holes

quiz.q: A paper is folded twice and a quarter circle is cut at the corner where both folds meet. What do you get?
quiz.explain: The 4 quarter circles join into one circle in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each layer gives a separate hole

quiz.q: How many layers are there after folding a paper 3 times?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, 4, 8.

quiz.q: Maya wants a square hole in the centre. What should she do?
options: Fold twice and cut straight across the folded corner
Fold once and cut a circle
quiz.explain: A straight cut across the twice-folded corner opens into a square.

quiz.q: A paper is folded once. On the fold, Ravi cuts a rectangle 1 cm wide (from the fold) and 2 cm long (along the fold). What hole does he get?
quiz.explain: The 1 cm width doubles to 2 cm when opened, so the hole is 2 cm by 2 cm, a square.

quiz.q: A paper folded twice has a small notch cut on one folded edge, not at the corner. How many notches or holes after opening?
quiz.explain: The 4 layers pair up across the fold, making 2 holes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every cut on 4 layers gives 4

teach.ask: Gappu folded paper twice and punched one hole in the middle. Gappu expected 1 hole but got 4. Explain.
teach.praise: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes! Now I can predict.
teach.nudge: How many layers does the paper have after two folds?

learn.hook: The word AMBULANCE is written back to front on the van. Why? Look in a car's mirror!
points: Place a mirror on a shape. If the shape and its reflection make the same shape, the mirror is on a line of symmetry.
Digits like 0, 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror held beside them.
A mirror also reverses the order of digits. So only numbers like 88, 101 and 808 look the same in the mirror.
AMBULANCE is written in mirror writing on the front of the van so drivers ahead can read it in their rear-view mirror.
You can try mirror writing in any script: write each letter flipped, starting from the other side.

example.q: Does 18 look the same in a mirror held beside it?
steps: 1 and 8 look the same in a mirror.
But the mirror swaps their order: 18 looks like 81.
So 18 does not look the same.

learn.reallife: Next time you see an ambulance, look at the front. The writing is reversed for the mirrors of cars in front!

games.title: Looks the same in a mirror held beside it?
items: MOM
WOW
CAT

items.text: AMBULANCE is reversed so drivers read it in their ___.
The digit ___ looks the same in a mirror.
Mirror writing starts from the ___ side.

quiz.q: Which number looks exactly the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 8 and 0 look the same in a mirror, and 808 reads the same from both ends.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the mirror reverses the order

quiz.q: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the van?
options: So only children can read it
So drivers ahead can read it in their mirrors
quiz.explain: A rear-view mirror flips the writing back to normal.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how mirrors flip words

quiz.q: How does the number 18 look in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 1 and 8 stay the same, but the order is reversed: 81.

quiz.q: Which word looks the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: W and O look the same in a mirror, and WOW reads the same both ways.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with non-symmetric letters

quiz.q: Hema puts a mirror across a heart shape. The heart and its reflection make the same heart. Where is the mirror?
quiz.explain: When a mirror shows the same shape, it is on the line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the mirror to symmetry

quiz.q: Which number made of 1s and 0s looks the same in a mirror?
quiz.explain: 1001 reads the same from both ends, and 1 and 0 look the same in a mirror.

quiz.q: Which of these digits does NOT look the same in a mirror held beside it?
quiz.explain: 3 flips and faces the other way. 0, 8 and 1 stay the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all digits stay the same

quiz.q: Sunil writes his name in mirror writing. How should he write?
options: Flip each letter and start from the other side
quiz.explain: Mirror writing flips each letter left to right and reverses the order.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mirror writing is upside down

teach.ask: Gappu wrote 18 and looked in the mirror. Gappu saw 81 and got confused. Explain.
teach.praise: The mirror swaps the order! Only numbers like 88 or 808 look the same.
teach.nudge: What does a mirror do to the order of digits?

topics.title: Symmetry of regular shapes on a dot grid

learn.hook: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry. Coincidence? Let's check other shapes!
points: A regular shape has all sides equal and all angles equal.
Regular triangle: 3 lines of symmetry. Square: 4. Regular pentagon: 5. Regular hexagon: 6.
For a regular shape, the number of lines of symmetry equals the number of sides.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2. A shape like a kite has 1.
On a dot grid, draw a shape and then test each possible fold line to find its lines of symmetry.

example.q: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
steps: For a regular shape, lines = sides.
So 6 lines of symmetry.

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, road signs and honeycombs often use regular shapes because they look balanced from every side.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
quiz.explain: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides and 5 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
quiz.explain: Regular shapes have as many lines of symmetry as sides.

quiz.q: A square has 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: 2 lines through the middles of sides and 2 diagonals: 4.

quiz.q: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A rectangle folds in half across and along, but not on its diagonals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rectangle are lines of symmetry

quiz.q: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: For regular shapes, lines of symmetry = number of sides.

quiz.q: On a dot grid, Sara draws a kite shape. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.explain: A kite folds into matching halves only along its long middle line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it has 2 like a rectangle

quiz.q: Which is true for regular shapes?
options: Lines of symmetry = double the sides
Lines of symmetry = number of sides
They have no lines of symmetry
quiz.explain: Triangle 3, square 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6.

quiz.q: How many more lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have than a regular triangle?

teach.ask: Gappu found a regular pentagon tile and wants to know how many ways it can be folded into matching halves. Explain.
teach.praise: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so 5 lines of symmetry!
teach.nudge: What is the link between sides and lines of symmetry in regular shapes?

learn.hook: Look at a bathroom wall. The same tile design repeats again and again. Can you find the smallest piece that repeats?
points: A tile pattern repeats a basic unit again and again.
To continue the pattern, find the unit and repeat it in the same way.
A tile can be slid (moved without turning), flipped (like a mirror) or turned (rotated) to make patterns.
A quarter turn rotates a tile by one right angle. Four quarter turns bring it back to the start.

example.q: A border goes ▲▼▲▼▲▼. What is the repeating unit, and which move changes ▲ into ▼?
steps: The unit is ▲▼.
▼ is ▲ flipped upside down (or turned half a turn).
example.answer: Unit ▲▼; a flip or half turn

learn.reallife: Sarees, bangles, temple floors and school walls all have tile patterns made by sliding, flipping or turning one design.

quiz.q: In the pattern ■●■●■●, what is the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ■● repeats again and again.

quiz.q: A tile is moved to the right without turning or flipping. What is this move called?
quiz.explain: Moving without turning is a slide.

quiz.q: A tile with an arrow → becomes ← . Which single move could do this?
quiz.explain: Flipping like a mirror changes → to ←. A half turn does too.

quiz.q: How many quarter turns bring a tile back to how it started?
quiz.explain: 4 quarter turns make a full turn.

quiz.q: What comes next? ▲▲▼▲▲▼▲▲
quiz.explain: The unit is ▲▲▼, so after ▲▲ comes ▼.

quiz.q: In ⭐🌙🌙⭐🌙🌙, how many shapes are in the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: ⭐🌙🌙 has 3 shapes.

quiz.q: A tile is turned a quarter turn each time: ↑ then →. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each quarter turn moves the arrow one right angle clockwise: ↑, →, ↓, ←.

quiz.q: A floor border uses the unit 🟥🟨🟨. How many 🟨 tiles are in 4 units?
quiz.explain: Each unit has 2 yellow tiles. 4 × 2 = 8.
steps: 4 units × 2 = 8

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tile a wall border with a pattern. Explain how to make one using a single tile.
teach.praise: I picked a unit and slid, flipped or turned it again and again. My border is ready!
teach.nudge: What do you repeat, and what moves can you use?

learn.hook: Bees build honeycombs with hexagons that fit perfectly. Why not circles?
points: Tessellation means covering a surface with shapes that leave no gaps and do not overlap.
Squares, rectangles, regular triangles and regular hexagons tessellate on their own.
Circles and regular pentagons leave gaps, so they do not tessellate on their own.
Some tiles in a shop are symmetrical, some are not. Look for a line of symmetry in each tile design.
You can join shapes to make a new tile that tessellates, or design your own tile with cut-outs or a rangoli kit.

example.q: Can circular tiles cover a floor without gaps?
steps: Circles touch only at points.
There are curved gaps between them.
So circles do not tessellate.

learn.reallife: Look at floors, footpaths and walls. Paver blocks and tiles fit together like a puzzle with no gaps!

games.title: Tessellation facts
items: Tessellating tiles leave no gaps.
That is the rule.
Tiles in a tessellation may overlap.
They must not overlap.
Honeycombs use hexagons, which tessellate.
Hexagons fit together with no gaps.
Two regular triangles joined make a shape that also tessellates.
They make a rhombus, which tessellates.
Every tile design in a shop is symmetrical.
Some designs have no line of symmetry.

quiz.q: What does tessellation mean?
options: Covering a surface with shapes with no gaps and no overlaps
quiz.explain: Tessellating shapes fit together completely.

quiz.q: Which shape does NOT tessellate on its own?
quiz.explain: Circles leave gaps between them.

quiz.q: Which shape do bees use in honeycombs?
quiz.explain: Regular hexagons fit together with no gaps.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that leaves gaps

quiz.q: Two regular triangles are joined side to side. Does the new tile tessellate?
quiz.explain: They make a rhombus, which fits with copies of itself.

quiz.q: A tile shows a flower with 4 equal petals. Is it symmetrical?
quiz.explain: A flower with 4 equal petals has lines of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for a fold line

quiz.q: Which is true about a regular pentagon?
options: It leaves gaps when tiled alone
quiz.explain: Regular pentagons do not fit together without gaps.

quiz.q: A floor is covered by 6 rows of 8 square tiles with no gaps. How many tiles?
Leena makes her own tile using a rangoli kit. What must be true for it to tile a floor?
options: Copies fit together with no gaps or overlaps
quiz.explain: A tessellating tile fits with its copies, leaving no gaps.

teach.ask: Gappu wants round tiles for the classroom floor. Explain why that may be a problem.
teach.praise: Round tiles leave gaps! Squares or hexagons fit perfectly.
teach.nudge: What happens between circles when you put them side by side?

topics.title: Floor patterns and the catty wall

learn.hook: Cut a bump from one side of a square and stick it on the opposite side. You get a cat-shaped tile that still fits!
points: A floor pattern is made by repeating one tessellating tile again and again.
Catty-wall trick: cut a piece from one side of a square and slide it to the opposite side.
The new tile has a funny shape (like a cat), but copies still fit together with no gaps.
The area stays the same, because nothing was thrown away: the piece only moved.
If the piece is not slid exactly to the opposite side, the tiles will not fit.

example.q: Raghav cuts a small triangle from the bottom of a square tile and sticks it on the top. Will copies fit together?
steps: The bump on top matches the gap at the bottom of the tile above.
So copies fit with no gaps or overlaps.

learn.reallife: Artists make animal-shaped tiles, like birds and fish, using this trick. Some famous tiles look like lizards!

games.title: Make a catty-wall tile
items: Start with a square
Cut a shape from one side
Slide the piece to the opposite side
Stick it there
Repeat the tile to cover the wall

games.title: Catty-wall facts
items: Sliding the cut piece to the opposite side keeps the tile tessellating.
The bump fits the gap of the next tile.
The new tile has a bigger area than the square.
The piece was only moved, so the area stays the same.
You can stick the piece anywhere and it will still fit.
It must go exactly opposite where it was cut.
A floor pattern repeats one tile again and again.
That is how tessellations work.
Animal-shaped tiles can tessellate.
If made by cutting and sliding, they fit together.

quiz.q: In the catty-wall trick, where does the cut piece go?
quiz.explain: The piece is slid to the opposite side so the tiles still fit.

quiz.q: After the catty-wall trick, how does the tile's area compare with the square's?
quiz.explain: Nothing is added or removed; a piece is only moved.

quiz.q: Why do the new cat-shaped tiles still fit together?
options: The bump on one side fills the gap on the next tile
quiz.explain: Each bump matches a gap, so there are no gaps or overlaps.
quiz.mistake: Does not see bumps and gaps match

quiz.q: What is a floor pattern made by?
options: Repeating one tile with no gaps
quiz.explain: A floor pattern repeats a tessellating tile.

quiz.q: Tanu cuts a piece from the left side of a square and sticks it on the TOP. What may happen?
options: The tiles may not fit together
quiz.explain: The piece must slide to the opposite side (right). Moving it elsewhere breaks the fit.

quiz.q: A wall needs 5 rows of 7 catty tiles. How many tiles?
A square tile has area 16 small squares. After the catty-wall trick, what is its area?
quiz.explain: Moving a piece does not change the area.
quiz.mistake: Adds or takes away the piece

quiz.q: Which shape is the best start for a catty-wall tile?
quiz.explain: Squares tessellate, so a cut-and-slide square still tessellates.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that does not tessellate

teach.ask: Gappu wants a wall full of cat-shaped tiles that fit with no gaps. How can Gappu make the tile?
teach.praise: Cut a bit from a square and slide it to the opposite side! Meow, it fits!

learn.hook: Look closely at a butterfly, a peepal leaf or a hibiscus flower. Nature loves symmetry!
points: Many living things are symmetrical: a butterfly's wings match, and many leaves match on both sides of the middle vein.
Some leaves are not symmetrical, like a torn leaf or a leaf with uneven sides.
Sort leaves into symmetrical and non-symmetrical by folding them along the middle vein.
Flowers with equal petals, like a 5-petal hibiscus, can have several lines of symmetry.
Use leaves and flowers dipped in paint to make prints for designs and greeting cards.

example.q: A flower has 5 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry might it have?
steps: Like a regular pentagon, a line can go through each petal.
So 5 lines.

learn.reallife: On a nature walk, collect fallen leaves and flowers. Fold them to test symmetry, then print them on a Diwali card!

games.title: Nature symmetry
items: A butterfly's two wings match.
Its body is the line of symmetry.
Every leaf is perfectly symmetrical.
Some leaves have uneven sides.
The middle vein of a leaf is often its line of symmetry.
The two halves match across it.
Leaf prints can be used to make greeting cards.
Paint the leaf and press it on paper.
A flower with 4 equal petals has no line of symmetry.
It has lines of symmetry through the petals.

quiz.q: Which part of a butterfly is its line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The body divides the butterfly into two matching halves.
quiz.mistake: Picks a part on one side

quiz.q: How can you test if a leaf is symmetrical?
options: Fold it along the middle vein and see if the halves match
quiz.explain: If the halves match when folded, it is symmetrical.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how to test

quiz.q: Which is most likely NOT symmetrical?
options: A leaf torn on one side
quiz.explain: The torn side no longer matches the other side.

quiz.q: A flower has 6 equal petals evenly spread. How many lines of symmetry can it have?
quiz.explain: Like a regular hexagon, it has 6 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: Riya collects 12 leaves. 9 are symmetrical. How many are not?
To make a leaf print card, what should you do?
options: Paint a leaf and press it on paper
quiz.explain: Painting and pressing makes a print.

quiz.q: A leaf print is made on one half of a folded card and the card is pressed shut. What appears on the other half?
options: A mirror image of the print
quiz.explain: The wet paint copies as a mirror image, like an ink blot.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect it with ink-blot designs

quiz.q: Which animal shows symmetry when seen from the front?
quiz.explain: A tiger's face has matching left and right halves.

teach.ask: Gappu found a leaf on a nature walk. How can Gappu check if it is symmetrical, and what can Gappu make with it?
teach.praise: Fold along the middle vein: the halves match! Now I will print it on a card.
